These provide decision-relevant evidence on separation mechanisms, impacts of PFAS and membrane properties, operating conditions, fouling, and when results are comparable across systems. Pure reviews and non-membrane adsorption studies were excluded as they do not offer primary, directly relevant quantitative data for membrane process selection.","component_coverage":[{"component_id":"RT04-C1","selected_source_ids":["D01","D02","D03","D06","D07","D08","D09","D11","D12","D14","D15","D16","D17"],"rationale":"RT04-C1 requires comparison of nanofiltration, reverse osmosis, adsorptive membranes, electrically assisted membranes, and hybrid configurations by separation mechanism. D01, D07, D08, D09, D11, D12, D14, D17, and D18 (indirectly via NF90 data) provide NF vs RO and NF-only performance and mechanism insights (steric hindrance, Donnan exclusion, solution–diffusion). D02 and D15 examine modified/TFN RO/NF-type membranes, allowing comparison of enhanced steric and electrostatic mechanisms. D06 and D16 are explicit adsorptive membrane studies (dual-function NF/adsorptive and pH-swing ion-exchange brushes), clarifying adsorption vs sieving contributions. D03 demonstrates FO driven by an NF support, giving hybrid FO–NF behavior. D09, D12, and D14 provide NF + adsorbent (GAC/IX) and NF + UV-sulfite hybrids, supporting comparison of separation roles within treatment trains. None of the selected studies is a dedicated electrically assisted membrane in the sense of driven by applied electric fields, so that subtopic remains a partial gap, but the rest of the component is well covered."},{"component_id":"RT04-C2","selected_source_ids":["D01","D02","D03","D07","D08","D09","D11","D12","D15","D16","D17","D18"],"rationale":"RT04-C2 focuses on how PFAS properties, membrane characteristics, operating conditions, co-ions, organic matter, and fouling affect performance. D02, D03, D07, D08, D09, D11, D12, D17, and D18 systematically vary PFAS chain length, functional groups, and concentration, as well as membrane MWCO, permeability, charge, and hydrophilicity, and report impacts of pressure/flux, recovery, and fouling. D02, D08, D09, D12, D16, and D18 explicitly examine ionic strength, specific ions (e.g., Ca2+, Mg2+, NaCl), and natural/effluent organic matter or co-contaminants, linking these to rejection and flux decline. D07 quantitatively correlates PFAS rejection and adsorption with molecular parameters (MW, logKow) and membrane MWCO and hydrophobicity, while showing weaker dependence on surface charge. D11 and D12 provide pilot-scale data on recovery, energy, and PFAS-specific rejection in groundwater matrices. D15 and D16 probe fouling, flux recovery, and water chemistry effects (ionic strength, NOM) on mixed-matrix and adsorptive membranes, extending coverage to adsorptive mechanisms under realistic matrices."},{"component_id":"RT04-C3","selected_source_ids":["D06","D07","D08","D09","D11","D12","D14","D17","D18"],"rationale":"RT04-C3 requires defining when reported rejection, adsorption, permeability, and energy data are comparable for process selection. D07, D08, D09, and D18 give explicit equations and protocols for calculating rejection (including handling of LOQ, single-pass vs effective rejection) and recovery, along with mass balances and adsorption-to-membrane quantification, which help distinguish true separation from apparent removal via sorption. D06 quantifies simultaneous NF rejection and adsorption in dual-functional membranes, clarifying how to interpret such data relative to purely size-exclusion processes. D11 and D12 provide pilot-scale RO and NF data with detailed operating conditions, specific flux/energy requirements, and recovery-dependent rejection, enabling assessment of when bench-scale and pilot-scale results are comparable. D14 and D17 present NF combined with GAC/anion exchange or green sorption media, carefully defining breakthrough, bed volumes, and overall removal, distinguishing membrane and adsorbent contributions—useful for comparing hybrid configurations. Collectively, these studies supply the methodological clarity needed to judge comparability of performance metrics across different membranes, operating regimes, and matrices."}]}

You are selecting primary PFAS treatment studies for a focused professional
review. You receive one task and an anonymized, BGE-ranked list of candidate
document cards.

Classify every candidate card. Select every document that is an independent
primary study, is directly relevant to at least one task component, and
contains extractable decision-relevant evidence. There is no target number of
selected documents and no penalty for retaining all eligible studies.

Eligible evidence includes:

- primary experiments, pilot or field deployments, and quantitative modeling
  or life-cycle studies;
- complementary matrices, PFAS scopes, operating regimes, endpoints, and
  scales;
- documents with concrete methods, conditions, results, limitations, residuals,
  energy, or cost evidence; and
- evidence that permits meaningful comparison or explains non-comparability.

Do not select a document merely because its title repeats task words. Do not
select reviews, perspectives, reference lists, duplicate records, or the
held-out defining review. Do not exclude an otherwise eligible study merely
because another selected study reports similar findings. Do not infer facts
absent from a card. Selection is document-level only: do not write the review
and do not score candidate answers.

Every candidate source_id must appear exactly once, either in
selected_source_ids or excluded_sources. Each required component must be
covered by at least one selected source. Return selected_source_ids in BGE rank
order.

Return one JSON object following the supplied schema exactly.

component_coverage.rationale: RT04-C1 requires comparison of nanofiltration, reverse osmosis, adsorptive membranes, electrically assisted membranes, and hybrid configurations by separation mechanism. D01, D07, D08, D09, D11, D12, D14, D17, and D18 (indirectly via NF90 data) provide NF vs RO and NF-only performance and mechanism insights (steric hindrance, Donnan exclusion, solution–diffusion). D02 and D15 examine modified/TFN RO/NF-type membranes, allowing comparison of enhanced steric and electrostatic mechanisms. D06 and D16 are explicit adsorptive membrane studies (dual-function NF/adsorptive and pH-swing ion-exchange brushes), clarifying adsorption vs sieving contributions. D03 demonstrates FO driven by an NF support, giving hybrid FO–NF behavior. D09, D12, and D14 provide NF + adsorbent (GAC/IX) and NF + UV-sulfite hybrids, supporting comparison of separation roles within treatment trains. None of the selected studies is a dedicated electrically assisted membrane in the sense of driven by applied electric fields, so that subtopic remains a partial gap, but the rest of the component is well covered.

RT04-C2 focuses on how PFAS properties, membrane characteristics, operating conditions, co-ions, organic matter, and fouling affect performance. D02, D03, D07, D08, D09, D11, D12, D17, and D18 systematically vary PFAS chain length, functional groups, and concentration, as well as membrane MWCO, permeability, charge, and hydrophilicity, and report impacts of pressure/flux, recovery, and fouling. D02, D08, D09, D12, D16, and D18 explicitly examine ionic strength, specific ions (e.g., Ca2+, Mg2+, NaCl), and natural/effluent organic matter or co-contaminants, linking these to rejection and flux decline. D07 quantitatively correlates PFAS rejection and adsorption with molecular parameters (MW, logKow) and membrane MWCO and hydrophobicity, while showing weaker dependence on surface charge. D11 and D12 provide pilot-scale data on recovery, energy, and PFAS-specific rejection in groundwater matrices. D15 and D16 probe fouling, flux recovery, and water chemistry effects (ionic strength, NOM) on mixed-matrix and adsorptive membranes, extending coverage to adsorptive mechanisms under realistic matrices.

RT04-C3 requires defining when reported rejection, adsorption, permeability, and energy data are comparable for process selection. D07, D08, D09, and D18 give explicit equations and protocols for calculating rejection (including handling of LOQ, single-pass vs effective rejection) and recovery, along with mass balances and adsorption-to-membrane quantification, which help distinguish true separation from apparent removal via sorption. D06 quantifies simultaneous NF rejection and adsorption in dual-functional membranes, clarifying how to interpret such data relative to purely size-exclusion processes. D11 and D12 provide pilot-scale RO and NF data with detailed operating conditions, specific flux/energy requirements, and recovery-dependent rejection, enabling assessment of when bench-scale and pilot-scale results are comparable. D14 and D17 present NF combined with GAC/anion exchange or green sorption media, carefully defining breakthrough, bed volumes, and overall removal, distinguishing membrane and adsorbent contributions—useful for comparing hybrid configurations. Collectively, these studies supply the methodological clarity needed to judge comparability of performance metrics across different membranes, operating regimes, and matrices.

result.selection_rationale: Most candidate documents are primary membrane studies that report PFAS rejection and/or adsorption under defined operating conditions, often with real or complex waters and, in several cases, hybrid configurations. These provide decision-relevant evidence on separation mechanisms, impacts of PFAS and membrane properties, operating conditions, fouling, and when results are comparable across systems. Pure reviews and non-membrane adsorption studies were excluded as they do not offer primary, directly relevant quantitative data for membrane process selection.
